## Natural history notes

A small leafhopper characterized by a wedge-shaped body, delicate roof-held wings, and greenish to yellowish or mottled coloration typical of sap-feeding cicadellids. In Florida, Tylozygus bifidus is recorded as part of the state’s leafhopper fauna and is most likely found in plant-rich habitats such as fields, roadsides, gardens, pine flatwoods, forest edges, and shrubby vegetation. Adults and nymphs feed by piercing plant tissue and drinking sap, while also serving as prey for spiders, assassin bugs, lacewings, birds, and parasitoid wasps.
